title: Why 'third party, fire & theft' covers less than most people think
excerpt: It sounds like the sensible middle option. It isn't — here's the one thing it never covers, whoever's fault an accident is.
body: Third party, fire & theft (TPFT) sits between the legal minimum and full comprehensive cover, and a lot of people assume it's simply 'comprehensive, but cheaper.' It isn't a smaller version of the same thing — it's missing one entire category of protection.

TPFT covers injury or damage you cause to other people, plus your own car if it's stolen or damaged by fire. What it never covers is damage to your own car from an accident that was your fault — or one where fault can't be proven. Reverse into a wall, and TPFT pays nothing towards your own repair bill.

That's the gap worth checking before picking TPFT to save money: is the saving worth being fully exposed on your own car's repair costs? For an older car worth less than a policy excess, that trade can make sense. For anything with real value, it usually doesn't.

Whichever level you're comparing, always read the IPID (Insurance Product Information Document) — it's a one-page, standardised summary every UK insurer has to provide, and it's the fastest way to see exactly what's excluded before you commit.
